checks.what: Carbonate δ¹³C climbs 5 ‰ above its Archean level between 2.25 and 2.0 Ga
checks.why: In the model the burst of phosphate from weathering long-buried sulfide rock comes right after the first rise of oxygen and is small, so carbon isotopes rise only a little, and too early. What drove the real shift of about +10 ‰ is still debated.

checks.what: Banded iron fades after oxygen rises (2.2 to 1.9 Ga under half of 2.6 Ga onward)
checks.why: Vents keep feeding iron into the model’s deep sea, and rust keeps forming where it meets oxygen near the surface. In the real ocean the deep water may have turned sulfidic, trapping the iron as pyrite; this model makes too little sulfate for that.
